findings.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:119 — `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` then `.integration` dereferenced **without** optional chaining (was `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`). Throws `TypeError` for any Google Meet booking where the organizer has no destination calendar — the exact case the branch exists to handle. `handleNewBooking.ts:1067` emits `null`; eight other call sites emit `[]`. Booking row is already committed at `handleNewBooking.ts:1952` and `eventManager.create` at :2114 is outside any try/catch → phantom booking blocking the slot. In the Stripe path the throw precedes `payment.update` → customer charged, booking never confirmed, webhook retries forever on the same deterministic crash.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1078 — `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a silent no-op when the field is `null` (lines 1063‑1067, i.e. no event-type and no organizer destination calendar) — the PR's headline feature does nothing in its most likely real-world configuration. No error, no log, reports success.

packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:221 — `createEvent` gained a **required** `credentialId` param, but only 1 of 4 implementations was updated (google). TS allows narrower implementations, so there is zero compile-time signal that lark, office365 and `BaseCalendarService` silently ignore it. Same for out-of-repo `Calendar` implementers — no `?`, no default, no deprecation.

packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:179 — CalDAV/Apple base filters `calendars` by `destinationCalendar[0].externalId` regardless of credential. For hosts 2..N the filter matches nothing → `Promise.all([])` → `responses.some(r => !r.ok)` is `false` → **returns a success object with a fresh uid for an event that was never created**. BookingReference persisted for a nonexistent event.

packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:73 — O365 (and lark `:128`) still build the URL from `destinationCalendar[0]` while authenticated as host N → 404/403. `CalendarManager.createEvent` returns `undefined` on 404 *before* `log.error`, so the failure is never logged; co-host silently gets no event.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:256 — Tautological fallback: `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : destinationCalendar?.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` — the `find` only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it can never match. `selectedCalendar` is always `undefined`, passed raw to `events.update({calendarId: undefined})` (:261) and `events.patch` (:277). Was `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. Every reschedule of a reference lacking `externalCalendarId` now fails.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:317 — Same dead `find` in `deleteEvent`, defaulted to `"primary"` at :322. Cancelling a booking on a non-primary destination calendar deletes nothing (404 swallowed as success) — the event stays on the host's calendar permanently.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:147 — `createEvent` now resolves the target by `cal.credentialId === credentialId`. `DestinationCalendar.credentialId` is nullable, and `EventManager` has an explicit branch for that case — so every user with a null-`credentialId` destination row now gets events written to **primary** instead of their selected calendar, silently, with a null `externalCalendarId` that makes it unfixable later.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:170 — `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined` — the non-calendar branch previously carried `result.credentialId`. All `*_video` BookingReferences now persist `credentialId: null`, and `handleCancelBooking.ts:491` gates `deleteMeeting()` on it → **Zoom/Teams/Cal Video rooms stay live and joinable after cancellation**, with the link already emailed to disinvited attendees. Unrelated to the stated intent.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:208 — `updateLocation` reads `result.externalId` / `result.credentialId`, but `CalendarManager.updateEvent` never sets either (only `createEvent` does). Both are always `undefined`; `editLocation.handler.ts:120` writes them into new references → every location edit produces references that can no longer target the right calendar.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:479 — `let credential` is function-scoped but assigned inside the new per-reference loop. When the DB hydration fails (deleted credential, or falsy `app?.slug`), it silently retains the **previous iteration's** credential and is passed to `updateEvent` at :542 → host B's event updated with host A's OAuth token. On the first iteration it is `undefined`, and `CalendarManager.updateEvent` dereferences `credential.appName` unconditionally. No `if (credential)` guard, unlike the sibling code at :369 and `handleCancelBooking.ts:442`.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:592 — The `catch` still builds `message` but `console.error(message)` was **deleted** — `message` is now dead and nothing is logged. Additionally `calendarReference` is only assigned at :495, so a throw before that returns `[]` via `?? []`. Callers gate on `results.some(res => !res.success)`, so a total failure to update every host's calendar reads as success, with no log line anywhere to diagnose it.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:369 — `if (credential) {...}` with no `else`: a host whose credential can't be hydrated is dropped from the fan-out with no `EventResult`, no log, no throw. `handleAppsStatus` records nothing, no BookingReference exists, so it can never be repaired by a later reschedule. Silent-pass by construction.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:454 — The recurring-cancellation block was moved *inside* the new per-reference loop but ignores `reference` entirely — still iterates only the organizer's credentials and still uses `references.find(...)` (singular). Co-hosts' events on every future recurrence are **never deleted**, while the whole organizer×occurrence sweep runs once per reference (N× Google API amplification, e.g. 4 hosts × 52 occurrences). `getCalendar(calendarCredential)` at :443 is dead work in this branch.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts:151 — `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` → `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` **inverts the condition** (the adjacent `requestedSlug` line kept its polarity, which makes it read as intentional). On cloud: an unverified, unpaid org immediately claims the globally-unique slug and `<slug>.cal.com`, and the collision check then locks out the legitimate owner. Self-hosted: orgs created with neither `slug` nor `requestedSlug` → unreachable. Entirely unrelated to this PR.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:339 — The fan-out `await`s `createEvent` per destination inside a `for` loop — no data dependency forces the order. On the user-blocking `POST /api/book/event`, a 5-host team goes from ~0.5s to ~2‑4s and a 15-host team to ~5‑12s of added latency, risking serverless timeouts *after* the booking row is committed but before `referencesToCreate` is persisted. `Promise.all` keeps wall time flat.

apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts:249 — `destinationCalendar` is spread into outbound webhook bodies (`{...evt}`), so this is an **unversioned breaking change** for subscribers reading `payload.destinationCalendar.externalId`. Worse, the empty representation is now inconsistent: `null` from `handleNewBooking`, `[]` from the eight other producers — the same underlying state serializes two different ways depending on which trigger fired. No version bump, no additive `destinationCalendars` field, no migration note.
packages/core/EventManager.ts:338 — Zero test coverage for the fan-out. `git ls-files

packages/core/EventManager.ts:344 — New `prisma.credential.findUnique({where:{id}})` (also :517) hydrates a credential — including `key`, the OAuth token — with **no `userId`/`teamId`/membership assertion**. The prior design was fail-closed (confined to `this.calendarCredentials`); it is now fail-open on an id read from a `DestinationCalendar`/`BookingReference` row. Because `getAllCredentials` excludes co-hosts' personal credentials, this is the hot path for the feature, not an edge case. A tenant-isolation guard was removed rather than replaced. *(Exploitability unproven — `setDestinationCalendar` validation not in this checkout.)*

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:433 — Same unscoped lookup on a path reachable by **anyone holding the booking uid** (unauthenticated attendee cancel link; the only gate is `userId !== bookingToDelete.user?.id && startTime < new Date()`). Hydrates an unverified credential and issues `deleteEvent` with it — and since new references may carry `externalCalendarId: undefined`, google falls back to `"primary"`.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1078 — Every co-host's full `DestinationCalendar` row (`externalId`, `userId`, `credentialId`) is now spread into outbound webhook bodies (:1754, :2296). Previously only the organizer's own. A team member with event-type webhook access harvests co-hosts' calendar and credential identifiers to an arbitrary endpoint.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:344 — N+1: per-destination `credential.findUnique` (+`app` join) inside the sequential loop, when all ids are known up front. Fires for essentially every non-organizer host. Same pattern at `EventManager.ts:517` and `handleCancelBooking.ts:433`.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:376 — The no-`credentialId` branch is now *inside* the per-destination loop and calls `createEvent(c, event)` without `externalId`: N legacy destinations × M organizer credentials → N×M calls, all falling back to `"primary"` (duplicate events on the organizer's own calendar), and `referencesToCreate` gets `externalCalendarId: undefined` where it previously got a real id — which then feeds findings #6/#7.
packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:168 — The insert uses `selectedCalendar \

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:2124 — `results.every(res => !res.success)` was written when there was at most one calendar result. With the fan-out, host 1 succeeding and hosts 2..N failing takes the **success** path — no error logged, confirmations sent. Partial fan-out failure is structurally invisible.

packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:242 — `success` is only flipped inside `.catch()`. If `getCalendar` returns null, `creationResult` is `undefined` but `success` stays `true` → a reference with `uid: ""` recorded as successful. `handleCancelBooking` now `.filter()`s all `_calendar` references, so it will later call `deleteEvent("")`.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:337 — No de-duplication by `externalId`/`credentialId`. Two hosts sharing a team calendar, or `eventType.destinationCalendar` equal to a host's, produce duplicate events and duplicate references — which then multiply update/delete traffic on every reschedule.

packages/features/ee/payments/api/webhook.ts:243 — `eventManager.create` runs before the payment/booking transaction with no `payment.success` idempotency guard. On Stripe redelivery what used to duplicate one calendar event now duplicates **N**, one per host, plus N more references. The sequential loop widens the window.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:99 — `new Promise(async (resolve, reject) => …)` — an async executor's rejection is discarded, so a rejected `getToken()` means the promise **never settles**. Pre-existing, but the fan-out turns it from a single-organizer risk into: one co-host with a revoked token hangs every collective booking until platform timeout, and later hosts are never attempted.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:470 — `apiDeletes.push(...)` creates live promises with no handler while the loop then `await`s DB/`getCalendar` for later references; `Promise.allSettled` isn't attached until :656 (and :619 does `await` on an *array*, which resolves immediately). A rejection landing in that window is an unhandled rejection. The loop widens this from one promise to N.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:735 — The `loadUsers` rewrite dropped `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` from the dynamic-booking select while the hosts branch retains it, so the function returns a union of two shapes. `IsFixedAwareUser` declares `organization: {slug: string}` as required and :870 papers over it with an unchecked cast → `getBookerUrl` produces non-org booker URLs in emails and event descriptions. Unrelated scope creep.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:344 — The 25-line "hydrate a credential and hand-rebuild it" block is duplicated verbatim at `EventManager.ts:343‑368` and `:516‑541`, with a third differently-shaped variant at `handleCancelBooking.ts:432‑441` (no `app` include, no reshaping — produces a credential with no `appName`). Any new field on `CredentialPayload` will be silently dropped by the hand-rebuilt copies with no compile error. Belongs in one `getCredentialById` helper.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:118 — "Array whose element 0 is secretly the main host" is an unenforced invariant re-narrowed ad-hoc at 8 sites across 6 files. Nothing in the type says index 0 is special, nothing guarantees non-empty, and `handleNewBooking.ts:1078` mutates the order by `push`. The author's own `@NOTE` comment flags it as a stopgap. An explicit `{organizer, others}` shape or one shared accessor would make finding #1 impossible.

packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:182 — New `schedulingType` on `CalendarEvent` is write-only — assigned once at `handleNewBooking.ts:1074`, never read anywhere. Because webhook bodies spread `...evt`, it leaks into public payloads from `handleNewBooking` only (absent on cancel/reject) — a new, undocumented, inconsistently-present public field. Also drags a Prisma-enum import into `packages/types`.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:987 — `teamDestinationCalendars` is filled as a **side effect** inside the `.map()` that builds `teamMembers`, then consumed 90 lines later. It only works because `.map` runs callbacks synchronously up to the first `await` — moving the push below `await getTranslation` or switching to `for await` would silently empty it.
packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:689 — `isTeamEventType` rewritten from compile-checked `SchedulingType.COLLECTIVE \

apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts:119 — Only 1 of 3 `destinationCalendar` assertions was migrated; :119 and :373 still assert `null` and still pass. The suite now actively cements two contradictory wire contracts for the same field, and `toMatchObject` means new payload fields (e.g. `schedulingType`) are unasserted.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:122 — Index 0 supplies the organizer attendee's `email` for *every* host's event. When `eventType.destinationCalendar` is set, index 0 is an event-type calendar belonging to no host — host N's event lists e.g. `…@group.calendar.google.com` as the organizer. `BrokenIntegrationEmail.tsx:88` names the broken app from index 0 too.

packages/types/EventManager.d.ts:26 — `externalId` is populated only by `createEvent`, never by `updateEvent`/`deleteEvent`, with no doc comment recording the asymmetry — the optional field is what let finding #10 compile cleanly. Making it required (or splitting create/update result types) would have caught it.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:998 — `firstName: ""` / `lastName: ""` added to the team-member literal, but `TeamMember` (`Calendar.d.ts:41‑46`) has neither field — always-empty excess properties, unrelated to this PR.

packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:230 — Cosmetic scope creep inflating a calendar bugfix: user-facing `"organiser"`→`"organizer"` in calendar event bodies (adjacent `// TODO: i18n` shows it's separate work), `orginalBookingDuration` rename, the `import type { Booking }` split, and a comment spelling fix. Collectively they make the genuinely risky changes (#15, #31) harder to spot.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:418 — Array-valued variables kept singular names (`bookingCalendarReference`, `calendarReference`), and `EventManager.ts:562` shadows the outer array with an inner singular `const calendarReference` of a different type in the same function — exactly the naming drift that produces first-element bugs.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:727 — `loadUsers` throws bare `new Error(...)` only to catch it 3 lines later; the `catch` tests for `HttpError`/`PrismaClientKnownRequestError` but not bare `Error`, so two specific actionable messages become an opaque `500 "Unable to load users"`.

goldens.comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.

Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled

The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` the new fallback logic in `updateEvent` is: `const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. This means `selectedCalendar` becomes `undefined` in the common case where callers don’t pass `externalCalendarId`, whereas the previous code correctly fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. That is a concrete correctness regression introduced by the diff; unless there is an unshown fallback later in the function, the Google API call will be made with an undefined/invalid calendarId and can fail for reschedules/updates that rely on destinationCalendar fallback.
